newsitem.title: FINLAND: Outokumpu CEO says confident about future.
newsitem.headline: Outokumpu CEO says confident about future.

text.p: Finnish metals and mining group Outokumpu Oy's CEO Jyrki Juusela said on Monday he was confident about the future despite a sharp fall in 1996 profits and an expected further fall in copper prices.
"The year 1996 was a difficult year for us in many ways," Juusela told a news conference.
"We are not nervous. On the contrary, we are confident about the future," he added.
Group profit before extraordinary items and tax fell to 229 million markka from 1.48 billion in 1995 and Outokumpu blamed weaker prices for all its main metals for the decline.

Juusela said Outokumpu's market conditions are expected to improve gradually this year. Prospects for particularly zinc and nickel prices were good in the next few years, but there was a risk that copper price would fall.
"(The price of) copper is (generally) forecast to rise during the next few years, but we think that there is a risk for a moderate fall in prices in coming years," Juusela said.
The stronger dollar was expected to support Outokumpu's earnings in 1997, he said. @

"The dollar is a very significant currency for us," he said, adding that a 10 percent change in last year's average dollar/markka exchange rate would mean roughly over 300 million markka in group groperating earnings, other variables excluded.

Outokumpu said earlier the average dollar exchange rate against the Finnish markka had risen five percent in 1996 on 1995. This had slightly reduced the negative effect on profitability of the fall in metals prices.
